You are executing Loop 3 ("build + outreach email") of a real cold-outreach web-design pitch pipeline, for exactly ONE business, in a real private GitHub repo. Stop after this one business — do not touch any other repo.

## Repo
https://github.com/PIIIX-org/texas-bar-texan-drive-in (private). The `dev` branch already has the full Loop-2 plan: brief.md, implementation.md, design-system.md, page-plans/ (home, the-bar, visit, whats-on), assets.md, user-flow.md, handling-protocols.md, github-workflow.md, README.md, skills-used.md.

Clone it, read ALL of those files first, and build faithfully to what they specify — implementation.md and page-plans are law. Do not re-invent the design direction ("Carhop Marquee / Gulf Channel" — mid-century drive-in signage + Gulf Coast palette); execute it.

## The business (already researched + approved at Gate A/B, do not re-research)
- The Texan Drive-In, Corpus Christi, TX — neighborhood bar
- Real public phone: **(361) 444-5522** — sourced from a wanderlog.com listing, already cited in brief.md. This IS allowed to appear in the built site as a real "Call" CTA (tel: link) per this pipeline's own rule: "Demo CTAs allowed (Call / Get quote) using public business phone/email from brief." Loop 2's planning docs used a "[PHONE]" placeholder deliberately (planning docs aren't the live site) — for the actual built site, use the real number above.
- No public email exists for this business — do NOT invent one, do NOT add an email CTA or contact form that implies an email exists. Contact is phone-only.
- No usable logo/photo assets were scraped (Facebook/Yelp exist but no clean brand assets) — check assets.md for what it decided; if it calls for AI-generated hero imagery, use the Pollinations MCP (free, no key — try tools named like `mcp__pollinations*` or `@pollinations/mcp`) for on-brand generated imagery, or fall back to a strong CSS/SVG-driven visual treatment if image gen isn't available. Never generate or use a photo of a real identifiable person.

## Build
- Stack: Next.js (App Router) + TypeScript + Tailwind + shadcn/ui, static marketing site, no backend/DB
- Implement the pages from page-plans/ faithfully: home, the-bar, visit, whats-on (or whatever page-plans/ actually contains — read it, don't guess)
- Mobile-first, fast, polished. Follow design-system.md's actual colors/type/spacing — do not substitute a generic template
- Mark clearly in the site footer or an /about note that this is a sales demo concept, not the business's live site (per pipeline rule: never imply it's already live on their domain)
- Use the `impeccable` skill and the `design-taste-frontend` skill while coding (invoke via the Skill tool) to keep this from reading as generic AI-SaaS output
- Use the shadcn MCP to add components correctly if available

## CI (required before PR review)
Add a minimal GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) that runs `npm ci && npm run build` on pull_request to `dev`. It must pass.

## Git workflow — IMPORTANT, do not skip
- Work on a feature branch (e.g. `feat/loop3-build`), NOT directly on `dev`
- Open a PR from that branch into `dev`
- Verify CI is green on the PR
- **Do NOT merge the PR.** Do NOT push anything to `prod`. This pipeline requires a human (not you, not me) to review and merge — that review is Gate C, which hasn't happened yet. Leave the PR open.
- Update repo topics: remove `pending-beta`, add `in-progress` while you work, then switch to `ready-for-review` once the PR is open and CI is green. Do NOT set `ready-for-outreach` — that only happens after human merge, which hasn't happened.

## QA evidence (must actually do this, not just claim it)
- Run the Next.js dev server locally and take screenshots of the home page at both desktop (~1440px) and mobile (~390px) widths — use the `browse` skill/gstack tooling if available, or Playwright/puppeteer if you have to install one minimally. Save screenshots into a temp path and report their paths back to me.
- Check for broken links/images
- Confirm locale is correct (en-US)

## EMAIL_DRAFT.md (required file, add to the PR)
Must include:
- 3 subject line options (English)
- A short, human-sounding email (not salesy AI tone) — mention something specific and true about the business (e.g. its strong review count/rating, being a real neighborhood fixture) and that it currently has no working website
- A placeholder link for the demo (e.g. `[DEMO LINK]` — no live deployment exists yet, that's fine)
- A soft CTA to chat, no fake urgency
- Do NOT claim the site is already live on their domain
- Run the `stop-slop` skill on it afterward to strip AI writing tells
- Do NOT include any email address for the business (none exists) — the draft is FROM the pitcher, addressed generically or via the phone/call CTA context, not implying the business has an email inbox this will land in. Note in the file itself how this draft is meant to be delivered given no public email exists (e.g. via a contact form, social DM, or in-person/phone follow-up) — be explicit and honest about this constraint rather than glossing over it.

## Also update
- skills-used.md — append what you actually used during the build (impeccable, design-taste-frontend, shadcn MCP, Pollinations MCP if used, stop-slop, etc.)

## Before you report back, verify yourself
- grep the whole working tree for email-shaped strings (`@` followed by a domain) — there should be ZERO except code artifacts like `@apply`/`@media`/import specifiers. Report this check explicitly.
- Confirm the only phone number anywhere is (361) 444-5522, nowhere else, and it matches brief.md's citation.

## Report back (final message)
- PR URL and CI status
- Screenshot file paths (desktop + mobile)
- Full EMAIL_DRAFT.md content
- Confirmation of the email/phone grep check above
- Anything you had to deviate from in implementation.md/page-plans and why

{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"SubagentStart","additionalContext":"PONYTAIL MODE ACTIVE — level: full

# Ponytail

You are a lazy senior developer. Lazy means efficient, not careless. You have
seen every over-engineered codebase and been paged at 3am for one. The best
code is the code never written.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No drift back to over-building. Still active if
unsure. Off only: "stop ponytail" / "normal mode". Default: **full**.
Switch: `/ponytail lite|full|ultra`.

## The ladder

Stop at the first rung that holds:

1. **Does this need to exist at all?** Speculative need = skip it, say so in one line. (YAGNI)
2. **Already in this codebase?** A helper, util, type, or pattern that already lives here → reuse it. Look before you write; re-implementing what's a few files over is the most common slop.
3. **Stdlib does it?** Use it.
4. **Native platform feature covers it?** `<input type="date">` over a picker lib, CSS over JS, DB constraint over app code.
5. **Already-installed dependency solves it?** Use it. Never add a new one for what a few lines can do.
6. **Can it be one line?** One line.
7. **Only then:** the minimum code that works.

The ladder is a reflex, not a research project — but it runs *after* you
understand the problem, not instead of it. Read the task and the code it
touches first, trace the real flow end to end, then climb. Two rungs work →
take the higher one and move on. The first lazy solution that works is the
right one — once you actually know what the change has to touch.

**Bug fix = root cause, not symptom.** A report names a symptom. Before you
edit, grep every caller of the function you're about to touch. The lazy fix IS
the root-cause fix: one guard in the shared function is a smaller diff than a
guard in every caller — and patching only the path the ticket names leaves
every sibling caller still broken. Fix it once, where all callers route through.

## Rules

- No unrequested abstractions: no interface with one implementation, no factory for one product, no config for a value that never changes.
- No boilerplate, no scaffolding "for later", later can scaffold for itself.
- Deletion over addition. Boring over clever, clever is what someone decodes at 3am.
- Fewest files possible. Shortest working diff wins — but only once you understand the problem. The smallest change in the wrong place isn't lazy, it's a second bug.
- Complex request? Ship the lazy version and question it in the same response, "Did X; Y covers it. Need full X? Say so." Never stall on an answer you can default.
- Two stdlib options, same size? Take the one that's correct on edge cases. Lazy means writing less code, not picking the flimsier algorithm.
- Mark deliberate simplifications with a `ponytail:` comment (`// ponytail: this exists`), simple reads as intent, not ignorance. Shortcut with a known ceiling (global lock, O(n²) scan, naive heuristic)? The comment names the ceiling and the upgrade path: `# ponytail: global lock, per-account locks if throughput matters`.

## Output

Code first. Then at most three short lines: what was skipped, when to add it.
No essays, no feature tours, no design notes. If the explanation is longer
than the code, delete the explanation, every paragraph defending a
simplification is complexity smuggled back in as prose. Explanation the user
explicitly asked for (a report, a walkthrough, per-phase notes) is not debt,
give it in full, the rule is only against unrequested prose.

Pattern: `[code] → skipped: [X], add when [Y].`

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | The ladder enforced. Stdlib and native first. Shortest diff, shortest explanation. Default. |

Example: "Add a cache for these API responses."
- full: "`@lru_cache(maxsize=1000)` on the fetch function. Skipped custom cache class, add when lru_cache measurably falls short."

## When NOT to be lazy

Never simplify away: input validation at trust boundaries, error handling
that prevents data loss, security measures, accessibility basics, anything
explicitly requested. User insists on the full version → build it, no
re-arguing.

Never lazy about understanding the problem. The ladder shortens the
solution, never the reading. Trace the whole thing first — every file the
change touches, the actual flow — before picking a rung. Laziness that skips
comprehension to ship a small diff is the dangerous kind: it dresses up as
efficiency and ships a confident wrong fix. Read fully, then be lazy.

Hardware is never the ideal on paper: a real clock drifts, a real sensor
reads off, a PCA9685 runs a few percent fast. Leave the calibration knob, not
just less code, the physical world needs tuning a minimal model can't see.

Lazy code without its check is unfinished. Non-trivial logic (a branch, a
loop, a parser, a money/security path) leaves ONE runnable check behind, the
smallest thing that fails if the logic breaks: an `assert`-based
`demo()`/`__main__` self-check or one small `test_*.py`. No frameworks, no
fixtures, no per-function suites unless asked. Trivial one-liners need no
test, YAGNI applies to tests too.

## Boundaries

Ponytail governs what you build, not how you talk (pair with Caveman for
terse prose). "stop ponytail" / "normal mode": revert. Level persists until
changed or session end.

The shortest path to done is the right path.
"}}

1	# Brief: The Texan Drive-In
2	
3	## Business
4	
5	- **Name:** The Texan Drive-In
6	- **Category:** Neighborhood bar
7	- **City:** Corpus Christi, Texas (Gulf Coast, South Texas)
8	- **Locale:** en-US
9	- **Current web presence:** None. The domain commonly associated with this business, thetexancorpuschristi.com, does not resolve (DNS failure). The only public presence is Facebook, Instagram, and third-party listings (Yelp, Wanderlog).
10	- **Public sources used for this plan:**
11	  - Yelp: https://www.yelp.com/biz/the-texan-drive-in-corpus-christi
12	  - Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/Thetexancorpuschristi/
13	
14	## Audience
15	
16	Two audiences share one page:
17	
18	1. **Locals deciding where to go tonight or this weekend.** Corpus Christi regulars, off-shift service and refinery workers, Gulf Coast retirees, and college-age locals from Texas A&M-Corpus Christi. They check a place on their phone standing in a parking lot or on a friend's couch, not at a desk.
19	2. **Visitors to the coast.** Padre Island and North Beach tourists and weekend boaters who want a real neighborhood bar, not a tourist-trap patio bar, and use Google Maps and Yelp to sort real places from staged ones.
20	
21	A third, non-visitor audience for this document specifically: **the owner**, deciding whether this plan is worth greenlighting a real build (Loop 3).
22	
23	## Offer
24	
25	A full night out under one roof: pool tables, darts, shuffleboard, a patio, and live bands on weekend nights. No cover-charge claims, no menu prices, no hours are asserted anywhere in this plan unless the owner confirms them; every unverified fact is bracketed (see Verified Facts below).
26	
27	## Geography and cultural tone
28	
29	Corpus Christi sits on the Gulf of Mexico, across the bay from Padre Island and North Beach. The tone for this business is coastal South Texas, not Hill Country and not West Texas: salt air, shrimp boats, bay wind, refinery lights on the water, blue-collar and off-shore-industry regulars mixed with beach tourists. Casual, direct, unpretentious. No cowboy-hat/honky-tonk cliches, no oil-derrick iconography, no Hill Country wildflower softness.
30	
31	## Verified facts (use only these; everything else is bracketed)
32	
33	- 4.3-star rating from approximately 510 Google reviews
34	- Popular neighborhood bar with pool tables, darts, and shuffleboard
35	- Has a patio
36	- Weekend live bands
37	- No functioning website; entire online footprint is Facebook, Instagram, Yelp, Wanderlog
38	
39	Anything not on this list (street address, hours, cover charge, phone, email, founding year, "regulars for decades," specific band genres) is a placeholder in every deliverable: `[STREET ADDRESS]`, `[HOURS]`, `[PHONE]`, `[BUSINESS EMAIL]`, `[CONFIRM WITH OWNER]`. **No phone number or email appears anywhere in this repo, real or invented.**
40	
41	## Conversion goal
42	
43	Get a visitor to decide tonight: see what's on, see what the room and patio look like, and get directions. There is no online ordering, table booking, or ticketing in v0. Secondary goal: get the owner to say yes to a real build in Loop 3.
44	
45	## Positioning (locked before design or copy)
46	
47	The Texan Drive-In is Corpus Christi's proven full-night-out bar (games, patio, live bands) with a reputation that already exists (4.3 stars, ~510 reviews) and a discoverability problem (no website, so it loses every "bar near me" search to competitors who have one). The site's job is to close that gap, not to invent a new brand.
48	
49	## Rejected directions
50	
51	Three directions were considered before locking the plan below. All three fit "a Texas bar" in general; none of them fit *this* bar specifically, which is the test this plan has to pass.
52	
53	1. **Generic Texas honky-tonk (barnwood, Lone Star flag, steer skull, string lights).** Rejected because it is the default look for any Texas bar plan an agent would produce without reading the brief closely, it would suit Melody Ranch in Waco or Texas T Pub in San Antonio just as well, and it ignores both the business's actual name and its coastal location entirely.
54	2. **Clean "modern gastropub" template (warm cream background, terracotta accent, high-contrast serif, three-column feature cards).** Rejected because it is the AI-slop default for any small-business site regardless of subject (see design-taste-frontend's premium-consumer palette warning), it would make a dive bar with pool tables and a patio band look like a downtown wine bar, and it actively works against the "unpretentious neighborhood bar" trust signal the reviews already establish.
55	3. **Nightlife/DJ-club direction (near-black background, single neon accent, glassmorphism cards, event-ticket UI).** Rejected because The Texan Drive-In is a pool-and-darts neighborhood bar with a patio band, not a cover-charge nightclub; a clubby UI would misrepresent the actual experience and would read as bait-and-switch to a first-time visitor standing at the door.
56	
57	**Direction locked instead:** a mid-century roadside drive-in marquee sign (keyed to the business's actual name) fused with Gulf-port materiality (keyed to Corpus Christi specifically, not "Texas" generically). Full rationale in `design-system.md`.
58	
59	## Non-goals for v0
60	
61	- No online ordering, reservations, or payment
62	- No database, auth, or CMS
63	- No invented contact information of any kind
64	- No claims about pricing, cover charges, or hours
65	
66	## Files in this repo
67	
68	See `README.md` for the file index and `skills-used.md` for process notes.

- Has a patio
- Weekend live bands
- No functioning website; entire online footprint is Facebook, Instagram, Yelp, Wanderlog

Anything not on this list (street address, hours, cover charge, phone, email, founding year, "regulars for decades," specific band genres) is a placeholder in every deliverable: `[STREET ADDRESS]`, `[HOURS]`, `[PHONE]`, `[BUSINESS EMAIL]`, `[CONFIRM WITH OWNER]`. **No phone number or email appears anywhere in this repo, real or invented.**

## Conversion goal

Get a visitor to decide tonight: see what's on, see what the room and patio look like, and get directions. There is no online ordering, table booking, or ticketing in v0. Secondary goal: get the owner to say yes to a real build in Loop 3.

## Positioning (locked before design or copy)

The Texan Drive-In is Corpus Christi's proven full-night-out bar (games, patio, live bands) with a reputation that already exists (4.3 stars, ~510 reviews) and a discoverability problem (no website, so it loses every "bar near me" search to competitors who have one). The site's job is to close that gap, not to invent a new brand.

## Rejected directions

Three directions were considered before locking the plan below. All three fit "a Texas bar" in general; none of them fit *this* bar specifically, which is the test this plan has to pass.

1. **Generic Texas honky-tonk (barnwood, Lone Star flag, steer skull, string lights).** Rejected because it is the default look for any Texas bar plan an agent would produce without reading the brief closely, it would suit Melody Ranch in Waco or Texas T Pub in San Antonio just as well, and it ignores both the business's actual name and its coastal location entirely.
2. **Clean "modern gastropub" template (warm cream background, terracotta accent, high-contrast serif, three-column feature cards).** Rejected because it is the AI-slop default for any small-business site regardless of subject (see design-taste-frontend's premium-consumer palette warning), it would make a dive bar with pool tables and a patio band look like a downtown wine bar, and it actively works against the "unpretentious neighborhood bar" trust signal the reviews already establish.
3. **Nightlife/DJ-club direction (near-black background, single neon accent, glassmorphism cards, event-ticket UI).** Rejected because The Texan Drive-In is a pool-and-darts neighborhood bar with a patio band, not a cover-charge nightclub; a clubby UI would misrepresent the actual experience and would read as bait-and-switch to a first-time visitor standing at the door.

**Direction locked instead:** a mid-century roadside drive-in marquee sign (keyed to the business's actual name) fused with Gulf-port materiality (keyed to Corpus Christi specifically, not "Texas" generically). Full rationale in `design-system.md`.

## Non-goals for v0

- No online ordering, reservations, or payment
- No database, auth, or CMS
- No invented contact information of any kind
- No claims about pricing, cover charges, or hours

## Files in this repo

See `README.md` for the file index and `skills-used.md` for process notes.

1	# Design System: The Texan Drive-In
2	
3	## The lane: "Carhop Marquee / Gulf Channel"
4	
5	Two real, specific sources, not "Texas" in general:
6	
7	1. **The business's own name.** "Drive-In" points to mid-century roadside Americana: porcelain-enamel marquee sign letters, carhop-era boomerang shapes, string-bulb lighting, chalkboard specials boards. This plan treats the marquee sign as the site's actual design system, not as a decorative texture.
8	2. **Corpus Christi as a Gulf port, not "Texas" as a state.** Bay water, salt air, channel markers and buoys, galvanized dock hardware, shrimp-boat and refinery light at dusk. This is coastal South Texas, distinct from Hill Country (Waco), the High Plains (Lubbock), and inland Gulf-adjacent-but-urban Houston.
9	
10	**Design read:** local marketing site for a neighborhood dive bar's owner and its Corpus Christi patrons, mid-century-signage x Gulf-port language, custom aesthetic (no named component-library look), built in Tailwind + shadcn primitives, restrained motion so it stays fast on a phone in a parking lot or on patio wifi.
11	
12	**Dials:** `DESIGN_VARIANCE: 7` (asymmetric, not gallery-symmetrical, but not chaotic either), `MOTION_INTENSITY: 4` (fluid CSS/Motion micro-interactions, no scroll-hijacking, no pinning, no parallax), `VISUAL_DENSITY: 4` (daily-app spacing; a bar site needs photos and warmth, not art-gallery emptiness or dashboard density).
13	
14	## Why this lane will not be reused in this batch
15	
16	The other four businesses in `texas-bars-batch-1` sit in different geography and different building/venue traditions, and none of them share this business's core identity hook (the drive-in name):
17	
18	- **Sheffield's Ice House, Houston** — an "ice house" is its own distinct Texas building type (screened-in, indoor/outdoor, built around a literal ice-cooling era), urban and inland relative to a Gulf-front bay town. Its lane should come from ice-house architecture, not drive-in signage.
19	- **Robbins Nest, Lubbock** — High Plains West Texas: wind, red dirt, cotton and cattle country, big flat sky. The opposite of a coastal port town; no marquee-sign or bay-water material logic applies.
20	- **Melody Ranch, Waco** — Central Texas ranch-and-music-venue heritage. Its own name points to ranch materiality (rope, hide, weathered barnwood), not roadside porcelain signage.
21	- **Texas T Pub, San Antonio** — "pub" implies an urban historic/River Walk-adjacent crossover identity, not a roadside carhop sign.
22	
23	If a future loop reaches for neon marquee letters, boomerang shapes, or teal-and-amber Gulf-dusk gradients for any of those four, that is a lane collision and should be caught in review.
24	
25	## Color (5 named hex values, one accent, one decorative-only secondary)
26	
27	| Name | Hex | Role |
28	|---|---|---|
29	| Bay Dusk | `#0E3A3E` | Primary background (dark base), evokes dusk over Corpus Christi Bay |
30	| Channel Ink | `#082226` | Darkest layer: footer, nav-on-scroll, depth. Replaces pure black. |
31	| Marquee Amber | `#E8A23C` | **The one interactive accent.** Every CTA, link, focus ring, hover state uses this and only this. Locked page-wide. |
32	| Seafoam Porcelain | `#ECEFE6` | Light-section background, card fills, dark-mode body text. Cool off-white (salt-bleached porcelain), deliberately not the warm cream/brass "premium-craft" palette family. |
33	| Buoy Red | `#D1452B` | **Decorative only, single use.** The channel-marker pin on the map embed and nowhere else. Never used on a CTA, link, or anything interactive, so it never competes with Marquee Amber. |
34	
35	Text on Bay Dusk/Channel Ink: Seafoam Porcelain at full opacity for headings, 80% for body. Text on Seafoam Porcelain sections: Channel Ink. No pure `#000000`, no pure `#FFFFFF` anywhere.
36	
37	## Type (three roles, three real self-hostable families)
38	
39	- **Display (marquee letters):** Roboto Slab, weights 700/900, tight tracking (`-0.01em` to `-0.02em`), used only for the wordmark treatment and H1/H2 headlines. Justified as a slab serif because the brief is a genuine vintage/heritage signage case (porcelain marquee letter sets were thick geometric slab/grotesque forms), not a default "creative brief = serif" reach. Not Fraunces, not Instrument Serif.
40	- **Body:** Archivo, weights 400/500. High x-height grotesque sans, reads clean on a phone screen in direct sun or a dim patio.
41	- **Utility/data (hours, nav labels, prices, map captions):** IBM Plex Mono. Stenciled dockside-crate lettering feel, ties to the Gulf-port half of the identity, used sparingly (labels and numbers only, never body paragraphs).
42	
43	Type scale (desktop / mobile): H1 `text-5xl md:text-6xl` / `text-4xl`; H2 `text-3xl md:text-4xl`; H3 `text-2xl`; body `text-base md:text-lg`, max width `65ch`; utility labels `text-xs uppercase tracking-[0.08em]` in Plex Mono, used at most once per three sections (eyebrow-restraint rule, see `implementation.md`).
44	
45	## Spacing scale
46	
47	Base unit 4px. Steps used: 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128 (px), mapped directly to Tailwind's default scale (`1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32`). No custom spacing tokens invented; the default scale is more than enough for a five-page marketing site. Section vertical padding: `py-16 md:py-24` (daily-app density, not gallery `py-32`+).
48	
49	## Corner-radius lock
50	
51	One system: sharp corners (`rounded-none` / `rounded-sm` max 4px) on cards and image frames, to read like porcelain sign panels and dock hardware, not soft consumer-app UI. Buttons are the one exception: full-pill (`rounded-full`), styled to read like a marquee push-button light switch. This two-part rule (panels sharp, buttons pill) is the entire radius system; nothing else varies.
52	
53	## Motion notes
54	
55	- **Signature moment:** the wordmark ("THE TEXAN DRIVE-IN") renders as individual backlit letter tiles. On first load only, it flickers on like a real porcelain marquee sign powering up (2-3 quick flickers over about 500-700ms, then settles steady-lit) and never repeats on scroll or revisit within a session. Motivated by hierarchy: it draws the eye to the one thing that carries the brand.
56	- **Scroll reveals:** simple `whileInView` fade-and-rise (Motion library, not GSAP) on section entry, one clean pass, no restart on re-scroll.
57	- **No scroll-hijacking, no pinning, no parallax, no marquee-text-loop.** A neighborhood bar site has to open fast on a phone with patio wifi; cinematic scroll choreography is the wrong tool here even though the "marquee" name invites it.
58	- Everything above `MOTION_INTENSITY 3` respects `prefers-reduced-motion`: the flicker-on collapses to instantly-steady, reveals collapse to instantly-visible.
59	
60	## Tone (voice, not visuals)
61	
62	Direct, concrete, unpretentious. Short sentences describing real things (pool tables, patio, live bands, 4.3 stars) over adjectives. No "elevate," "unleash," "seamless," no em dashes anywhere, no invented superlatives ("best bar in Texas"). See `page-plans/` for the actual copy and `skills-used.md` for the copy process.
63	
64	## What this is not
65	
66	Not a honky-tonk template (no barnwood, Lone Star flag, steer skulls). Not a "modern gastropub" cream-and-terracotta template. Not a nightclub/DJ template (no glassmorphism, no cover-charge ticketing UI, no near-black-with-neon-glow AI-purple look). See `brief.md` for the three rejected directions and why.
67

- **Robbins Nest, Lubbock** — High Plains West Texas: wind, red dirt, cotton and cattle country, big flat sky. The opposite of a coastal port town; no marquee-sign or bay-water material logic applies.
- **Melody Ranch, Waco** — Central Texas ranch-and-music-venue heritage. Its own name points to ranch materiality (rope, hide, weathered barnwood), not roadside porcelain signage.
- **Texas T Pub, San Antonio** — "pub" implies an urban historic/River Walk-adjacent crossover identity, not a roadside carhop sign.

If a future loop reaches for neon marquee letters, boomerang shapes, or teal-and-amber Gulf-dusk gradients for any of those four, that is a lane collision and should be caught in review.

## Color (5 named hex values, one accent, one decorative-only secondary)

| Name | Hex | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Bay Dusk | `#0E3A3E` | Primary background (dark base), evokes dusk over Corpus Christi Bay |
| Channel Ink | `#082226` | Darkest layer: footer, nav-on-scroll, depth. Replaces pure black. |
| Marquee Amber | `#E8A23C` | **The one interactive accent.** Every CTA, link, focus ring, hover state uses this and only this. Locked page-wide. |
| Seafoam Porcelain | `#ECEFE6` | Light-section background, card fills, dark-mode body text. Cool off-white (salt-bleached porcelain), deliberately not the warm cream/brass "premium-craft" palette family. |
| Buoy Red | `#D1452B` | **Decorative only, single use.** The channel-marker pin on the map embed and nowhere else. Never used on a CTA, link, or anything interactive, so it never competes with Marquee Amber. |

Text on Bay Dusk/Channel Ink: Seafoam Porcelain at full opacity for headings, 80% for body. Text on Seafoam Porcelain sections: Channel Ink. No pure `#000000`, no pure `#FFFFFF` anywhere.

## Type (three roles, three real self-hostable families)

- **Display (marquee letters):** Roboto Slab, weights 700/900, tight tracking (`-0.01em` to `-0.02em`), used only for the wordmark treatment and H1/H2 headlines. Justified as a slab serif because the brief is a genuine vintage/heritage signage case (porcelain marquee letter sets were thick geometric slab/grotesque forms), not a default "creative brief = serif" reach. Not Fraunces, not Instrument Serif.
- **Body:** Archivo, weights 400/500. High x-height grotesque sans, reads clean on a phone screen in direct sun or a dim patio.
- **Utility/data (hours, nav labels, prices, map captions):** IBM Plex Mono. Stenciled dockside-crate lettering feel, ties to the Gulf-port half of the identity, used sparingly (labels and numbers only, never body paragraphs).

Type scale (desktop / mobile): H1 `text-5xl md:text-6xl` / `text-4xl`; H2 `text-3xl md:text-4xl`; H3 `text-2xl`; body `text-base md:text-lg`, max width `65ch`; utility labels `text-xs uppercase tracking-[0.08em]` in Plex Mono, used at most once per three sections (eyebrow-restraint rule, see `implementation.md`).

## Spacing scale

Base unit 4px. Steps used: 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128 (px), mapped directly to Tailwind's default scale (`1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32`). No custom spacing tokens invented; the default scale is more than enough for a five-page marketing site. Section vertical padding: `py-16 md:py-24` (daily-app density, not gallery `py-32`+).

## Corner-radius lock

One system: sharp corners (`rounded-none` / `rounded-sm` max 4px) on cards and image frames, to read like porcelain sign panels and dock hardware, not soft consumer-app UI. Buttons are the one exception: full-pill (`rounded-full`), styled to read like a marquee push-button light switch. This two-part rule (panels sharp, buttons pill) is the entire radius system; nothing else varies.

## Motion notes

- **Signature moment:** the wordmark ("THE TEXAN DRIVE-IN") renders as individual backlit letter tiles. On first load only, it flickers on like a real porcelain marquee sign powering up (2-3 quick flickers over about 500-700ms, then settles steady-lit) and never repeats on scroll or revisit within a session. Motivated by hierarchy: it draws the eye to the one thing that carries the brand.
- **Scroll reveals:** simple `whileInView` fade-and-rise (Motion library, not GSAP) on section entry, one clean pass, no restart on re-scroll.
- **No scroll-hijacking, no pinning, no parallax, no marquee-text-loop.** A neighborhood bar site has to open fast on a phone with patio wifi; cinematic scroll choreography is the wrong tool here even though the "marquee" name invites it.
- Everything above `MOTION_INTENSITY 3` respects `prefers-reduced-motion`: the flicker-on collapses to instantly-steady, reveals collapse to instantly-visible.

## Tone (voice, not visuals)

Direct, concrete, unpretentious. Short sentences describing real things (pool tables, patio, live bands, 4.3 stars) over adjectives. No "elevate," "unleash," "seamless," no em dashes anywhere, no invented superlatives ("best bar in Texas"). See `page-plans/` for the actual copy and `skills-used.md` for the copy process.

## What this is not

Not a honky-tonk template (no barnwood, Lone Star flag, steer skulls). Not a "modern gastropub" cream-and-terracotta template. Not a nightclub/DJ template (no glassmorphism, no cover-charge ticketing UI, no near-black-with-neon-glow AI-purple look). See `brief.md` for the three rejected directions and why.

2	
3	## File and folder naming
4	
5	- Root-level plan files stay flat (`brief.md`, `implementation.md`, `design-system.md`, `assets.md`, `user-flow.md`, `handling-protocols.md`, `github-workflow.md`, `README.md`, `skills-used.md`), matching this loop's required list. Do not nest them into a `docs/` folder; the required-files list treats them as repo-root documents.
6	- `page-plans/` holds one file per route, named after the route slug, not the nav label: `home.md`, `the-bar.md`, `whats-on.md`, `visit.md`. If a page is added later, add one file named after its URL slug; do not batch multiple pages into one file.
7	- When Loop 3 adds real code, it goes in the conventional Next.js layout (`app/`, `components/`, `lib/`, `public/`); this repo has none of that yet by design, since Loop 2 is plan-only.
8	
9	## On context loss / resuming after interruption
10	
11	1. Read `README.md` first for current status.
12	2. Read `brief.md` for the verified-facts list before touching any copy; never re-derive facts from memory or assumption.
13	3. Check the open PRs and the `dev` branch history (`github-workflow.md`) to see what Loop 3 work, if any, is in flight.
14	4. If picking this up mid-Loop-3-build, re-read `implementation.md` in full before writing code; it is written to remove the need to ask questions, so re-reading it is cheaper than re-deciding anything it already answers.
15	5. Never re-research the business. This plan was built from Gate-A-approved research; if something looks wrong or missing, flag it for a human rather than re-scraping Yelp/Facebook independently.
16	
17	## Multi-agent handoff
18	
19	- Loop 2 (this repo's plan content) and Loop 3 (the actual build) are expected to run as separate agent sessions, possibly different agents entirely. `implementation.md` is written as the complete handoff document; an agent starting Loop 3 should need nothing beyond this repo's files plus normal Next.js/Tailwind/shadcn knowledge.
20	- If multiple agents work Loop 3 in parallel (e.g., one per page), each should work off its own `page-plans/<slug>.md` file and the shared `design-system.md`/`implementation.md` tokens, to avoid two agents inventing two different color systems.
21

23	
24	- Use the `/browse` skill (gstack) for any visual QA of the built site once Loop 3 produces one; do not use `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*` tools, per this account's standing instruction.
25	- Test both `prefers-color-scheme` states and `prefers-reduced-motion` on and off before calling a build done, per `implementation.md`'s definition of done.
26	- Test the hero and nav specifically at a narrow mobile width first (this audience is overwhelmingly mobile per `user-flow.md`), then desktop.
27

29	
30	- This plan intentionally caps the page count at four (`home`, `the-bar`, `whats-on`, `visit`) and the component list at thirteen named, reused components (see `implementation.md`), so a Loop 3 build agent has a small, closed surface to implement rather than an open-ended one.

33	- When resuming a stalled Loop 3 session, read `implementation.md` and the relevant single `page-plans/<slug>.md` file, not the whole repo, unless the task is genuinely repo-wide (e.g., a global palette change).

1	# Skills used, and why
2	
3	## Ideation
4	
5	No installed "ADHD"/diverge-score-prune-deepen skill was available in this environment. In its place: three concrete positioning/homepage directions were drafted, scored against the brief, and two were rejected in writing (see `brief.md` -> Rejected directions): a generic Texas honky-tonk template, a clean modern-gastropub template, and a nightlife/DJ-club template. The one locked (Carhop Marquee / Gulf Channel) is the one direction keyed to this business's actual name and actual city rather than "a Texas bar" in general.
6	
7	## Design direction
8	
9	- **`frontend-design:frontend-design`** - invoked with the full brief before locking any layout or color. Produced the brainstorm-then-critique discipline used to pick the "marquee sign as literal design system" signature element, and the reminder to name a compact color/type/layout/signature token system before writing anything else. Applied in `design-system.md` and the layout notes in `page-plans/home.md`.
10	- **`design-taste-frontend`** - invoked to audit the candidate lane for genericness before locking it. Its output shaped several concrete constraints applied throughout: the premium-consumer beige+brass palette ban (used to justify why Seafoam Porcelain and Bay Dusk were chosen over a cream/terracotta palette), the one-accent-color lock (Marquee Amber as the only interactive accent, Buoy Red restricted to one decorative, non-interactive use), the eyebrow-restraint rule (checked explicitly at the end of each `page-plans/*.md` file), the hero-stack-discipline cap (checked in `page-plans/home.md`), the zigzag/section-repetition caps (checked per page), and the zero-em-dash rule (verified by grep across every file before commit, see below).
11	
12	## Copy / writing
13	
14	- **`copywriting`** - invoked with the real facts (4.3 stars, ~510 reviews, pool/darts/shuffleboard, patio, weekend bands) and the no-invented-contact-info constraint, to structure the hero headline/subhead/CTA and three section headline/subhead pairs around benefits and specifics rather than adjectives.
15	- **`ogilvy`** - invoked to pressure-test the headline against Ogilvy's positioning-then-promise hierarchy and headline rules (brand + promise, specificity over cleverness). Result: the brand name lives in the visual marquee wordmark rather than being repeated in the H1 text, and the H1 instead delivers the promise in plain, factual language ("Pool, Darts, Shuffleboard, a Patio, and Live Bands on Weekends").
16	- **`stop-slop`** - invoked against the drafted homepage copy blocks (hero + three condensed sections) before they were committed, and again in a second pass against every `page-plans/*.md` file after an advisor review flagged that the first pass had not covered the sub-pages. Confirmed problems found and fixed, by file:
17	  - `page-plans/home.md`: a "Here's what's on tonight" throat-clearing construction in the hero subhead; an unverifiable invented claim ("Corpus Christi has been coming back for years") in the reviews section; an unverified claim about ticket/cover policy ("No Ticket Required") in the live-music headline.
18	  - `page-plans/whats-on.md`: a reintroduced pricing claim ("Nothing to buy in advance") that contradicted the file's own stated no-pricing-claim rule; an unverified band-origin claim ("Local Bands"); a "Not X. It's Y." binary-contrast pattern; a "Here's how to find us" throat-clearer.
19	  - `page-plans/the-bar.md`: a "[Noun]. That's it." dramatic-fragmentation headline ("Not Fancy. That's the Point.").
20	  - `page-plans/visit.md`: a fabricated geographic detail ("On the water side of Corpus Christi", no address is confirmed) and a city-personification headline ("What Corpus Christi Says").
21	  All are corrected in the copy that actually shipped. The lesson carried into `implementation.md` and `handling-protocols.md`: a style pass on the hero does not cover copy drafted later for other pages; every page needs its own pass, not just the first one written.
22	
23	## Diagrams
24	
25	- **`diagram-design`** was considered for `user-flow.md` but its output format is a standalone HTML file with inline SVG, which does not fit a Markdown deliverable meant to live and render in a GitHub repo. Hand-wrote two Mermaid flowcharts instead (visitor flow and owner flow), which render natively on GitHub and stay in the same file format as every other deliverable in this repo. Noted here per the task's "diagram-design or hand-write" option.
26	
27	## Research / assets
28	
29	No live browsing of Yelp or Facebook was performed for this plan: both are known to restrict headless scraping, this is a planning loop (not a build loop), and the task explicitly says not to re-research the Gate-A-approved lead. `assets.md` instead documents what exists at those two URLs as a Loop-3 harvest-with-rights-check task, and gives ready-to-use Pollinations prompts (free, keyless) for every image this v0 site actually needs.
30	
31	## Self-score (target ≥ 90/100)
32	
33	| # | Dimension | Score /10 | Notes |
34	|---|---|---|---|
35	| 1 | Positioning clarity | 9 | Locked in `brief.md` before any design/copy work: "proven full-night-out bar losing every 'bar near me' search to a competitor with a website." |
36	| 2 | Unique visual direction | 9 | Carhop Marquee / Gulf Channel lane keyed to the literal business name and Corpus Christi's Gulf-port geography, not "Texas" in general; explicit non-overlap argument against all four other batch businesses in `design-system.md`. |
37	| 3 | Strengths reflected on homepage | 9 | 4.3 stars / ~510 reviews, pool/darts/shuffleboard, patio, weekend live bands all appear in the hero or the first three homepage sections. |
38	| 4 | Weaknesses addressed | 9 | No-website problem is the whole site's reason to exist; trust handled via real stat + outbound links to the existing Yelp/Facebook presence rather than invented testimonials; one CTA label per intent; explicit mobile-first hero and nav rules. |
39	| 5 | Page-by-page IA | 9 | Four routes (`home`, `the-bar`, `whats-on`, `visit`) map directly to this business's actual features (games, patio, live-band schedule, directions), not a generic template IA. |
40	| 6 | Component inventory | 9 | Thirteen named, reused components specified per page in `implementation.md` and `page-plans/`; one naming inconsistency (an ad hoc "CTA band") was caught in review and resolved by explicitly documenting it as a text+shared-Button pattern rather than a fourteenth component. |
41	| 7 | Copy direction + locale | 9 | Real, fact-checked en-US copy for every section; passed through `stop-slop` in two rounds (homepage, then every sub-page after an advisor review caught the gap), ten concrete AI-tell/accuracy problems found and fixed across four files (see above), zero em dashes (verified by grep). |
42	| 8 | Asset list completeness | 9 | Existing-but-rights-gated sources (Facebook, Yelp) separated clearly from what must be generated, with ready-to-run Pollinations prompts per placement and an explicit no-fake-crowd-faces rule. |
43	| 9 | implementation.md executable without questions | 9 | Fixed stack, fixed four routes, fixed thirteen-component list, pre-written JSON-LD block that omits unconfirmed contact fields entirely (rather than emitting a bracket placeholder a search engine would parse as real data), explicit performance/mobile/definition-of-done sections. |
44	| 10 | Repo hygiene | 9 | README with status/campaign/pickup instructions, all ten required files present and verified on GitHub, `dev` default + empty `prod` branch pointing at the same initial commit, topics applied including the documented `geo-texas` substitution for GitHub's colon restriction. |
45	
46	**Total: 90/100** on the honest first-pass read. A second pass followed anyway, prompted by an advisor review rather than a low score: it found and fixed a real gap the first-pass numbers above did not catch (`stop-slop` had only been run against the homepage copy, not the three sub-pages drafted afterward, which had let a contradicted pricing claim, a fabricated address detail, and two banned rhetorical patterns ship). That fix is reflected in dimension 7's note and in the copy that actually shipped. No dimension scored a 10, since a repo that has not yet been built and used by an owner has not earned a perfect score on any axis, including hygiene.

The literal digital marquee. This page's entire job is to answer one question fast: is there a band tonight or this weekend, and when.

## 1. Sub-hero

- **Headline:** "This Weekend on the Patio."
- **Subhead:** "Bands play most weekend nights. Show up and grab a seat."
- **No claim about tickets, cover charge, or price anywhere on this page; neither is verified.** The subhead above is worded to avoid implying either one.

## 2. The marquee board (the site's signature component, doing real work here)

- **Component:** `MarqueeBoard`, full-size version (the homepage teaser was the small version of the same component; this is the one place it appears at full scale)
- Behavior: each row is one date, styled as a physical marquee letter-board row (Plex Mono for the date/day label, Roboto Slab for the act name). If no real schedule data exists at build time, every row ships as `[CONFIRM WITH OWNER: Friday/Saturday act name]` rather than an invented band name or genre
- Data source note for Loop 3: this is a static/manually-updated list in v0 (a simple array in the page, or a single JSON file the owner can edit), not a booking system or CMS; see `implementation.md`

## 3. What kind of nights these are

- **Headline:** "A Full Patio, a Band, No Fuss."
- **Subhead:** "It's a neighborhood patio with a band on it, not a concert hall." (No claims about band origin, e.g. "local," or genre, e.g. "country," "rock," unless the owner confirms; the copy stays unspecified on purpose.)
- **Component:** `PhotoFeatureRow`, image of the patio at night/dusk (ties visually to the hero's gulf-dusk gradient)

## 4. Directions CTA

- **Text:** "Already decided? Find directions below."
- **CTA:** "Get Directions" -> `/visit#map` (same label/intent as the homepage secondary CTA)

## Section-layout-repetition check

`PageIntro`, `MarqueeBoard` (unique to this page at full scale), `PhotoFeatureRow`, CTA band: four sections, no two sharing a family beyond the one intentional `PhotoFeatureRow` reuse (which appears once here and once on `/the-bar`, never back-to-back on the same page).

# Page plan: Visit (`/visit`)

The final step in the flow from `user-flow.md`: the visitor is sold, now they need logistics. This page is the closest thing to a "contact page" this site has, and it deliberately has no contact form, phone number, or email address.

## 1. Sub-hero

- **Headline:** "Find The Texan Drive-In."
- **Subhead:** "Corpus Christi, Texas. Full directions and hours below."

## 2. Map

- **Component:** `MapEmbed`, anchor id `#map`, embedded map (e.g., Google Maps iframe) centered on `[STREET ADDRESS]` once the owner confirms it; ships with a placeholder pin over a generic Corpus Christi map view until then, clearly labeled in code comments as `TODO: replace with confirmed address`
- **Decorative detail:** the map pin uses `Buoy Red` (`#D1452B`), the one approved use of that color on the whole site, styled like a small channel-marker buoy rather than a generic teardrop pin
- **CTA:** "Open in Google Maps" (deep link, opens the visitor's own maps app with the address once confirmed)

## 3. Hours

- **Component:** `HoursTable` (simple two-column list, not a dense bordered table), all seven rows ship as `[HOURS: CONFIRM WITH OWNER]` until real hours exist. No invented hours, ever, including "typical bar hours."

## 4. Reviews and trust (the full version; the homepage carried the condensed teaser)

- **Headline:** "What the Reviews Say."
- **Component:** `ReviewGrid`, 4.3-star stat displayed large (Roboto Slab numeral, not a filled progress-bar widget), "~510 Google reviews" as the supporting line, plus outbound links to the Yelp listing and the Facebook page. Review excerpt cards ship only with owner-approved or verifiably public text; otherwise the section ships as stat-plus-links only, no placeholder quotes invented to fill space.

## 5. Follow along

- **Headline:** "Between Visits, Follow the Patio."
- **Component:** social link row, Facebook and Instagram, icon + label, no follower counts claimed unless verified

## Section-layout-repetition check

`PageIntro`, `MapEmbed`, `HoursTable`, `ReviewGrid`, social row: five sections, five distinct families, no repetition.

## Explicit no-invention rule for this page

This is the page most tempted to fabricate a phone number, email, or hours "to look complete." It must not. Every unconfirmed field ships bracketed and visible as unconfirmed, not silently filled with a plausible-looking fake value. This rule is restated in `implementation.md` so the Loop 3 build agent cannot miss it.

# Brief: The Texan Drive-In

## Business

- **Name:** The Texan Drive-In
- **Category:** Neighborhood bar
- **City:** Corpus Christi, Texas (Gulf Coast, South Texas)
- **Locale:** en-US
- **Current web presence:** None. The domain commonly associated with this business, thetexancorpuschristi.com, does not resolve (DNS failure). The only public presence is Facebook, Instagram, and third-party listings (Yelp, Wanderlog).
- **Public sources used for this plan:**
  - Yelp: https://www.yelp.com/biz/the-texan-drive-in-corpus-christi
  - Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/Thetexancorpuschristi/

## Audience

Two audiences share one page:

1. **Locals deciding where to go tonight or this weekend.** Corpus Christi regulars, off-shift service and refinery workers, Gulf Coast retirees, and college-age locals from Texas A&M-Corpus Christi. They check a place on their phone standing in a parking lot or on a friend's couch, not at a desk.
2. **Visitors to the coast.** Padre Island and North Beach tourists and weekend boaters who want a real neighborhood bar, not a tourist-trap patio bar, and use Google Maps and Yelp to sort real places from staged ones.

A third, non-visitor audience for this document specifically: **the owner**, deciding whether this plan is worth greenlighting a real build (Loop 3).

## Offer

A full night out under one roof: pool tables, darts, shuffleboard, a patio, and live bands on weekend nights. No cover-charge claims, no menu prices, no hours are asserted anywhere in this plan unless the owner confirms them; every unverified fact is bracketed (see Verified Facts below).

## Geography and cultural tone

Corpus Christi sits on the Gulf of Mexico, across the bay from Padre Island and North Beach. The tone for this business is coastal South Texas, not Hill Country and not West Texas: salt air, shrimp boats, bay wind, refinery lights on the water, blue-collar and off-shore-industry regulars mixed with beach tourists. Casual, direct, unpretentious. No cowboy-hat/honky-tonk cliches, no oil-derrick iconography, no Hill Country wildflower softness.

## Verified facts (use only these; everything else is bracketed)

- 4.3-star rating from approximately 510 Google reviews
- Popular neighborhood bar with pool tables, darts, and shuffleboard
- Has a patio
- Weekend live bands
- No functioning website; entire online footprint is Facebook, Instagram, Yelp, Wanderlog

Anything not on this list (street address, hours, cover charge, phone, email, founding year, "regulars for decades," specific band genres) is a placeholder in every deliverable: `[STREET ADDRESS]`, `[HOURS]`, `[PHONE]`, `[BUSINESS EMAIL]`, `[CONFIRM WITH OWNER]`. **No phone number or email appears anywhere in this repo, real or invented.**

## Conversion goal

Get a visitor to decide tonight: see what's on, see what the room and patio look like, and get directions. There is no online ordering, table booking, or ticketing in v0. Secondary goal: get the owner to say yes to a real build in Loop 3.

## Positioning (locked before design or copy)

The Texan Drive-In is Corpus Christi's proven full-night-out bar (games, patio, live bands) with a reputation that already exists (4.3 stars, ~510 reviews) and a discoverability problem (no website, so it loses every "bar near me" search to competitors who have one). The site's job is to close that gap, not to invent a new brand.

## Rejected directions

Three directions were considered before locking the plan below. All three fit "a Texas bar" in general; none of them fit *this* bar specifically, which is the test this plan has to pass.

1. **Generic Texas honky-tonk (barnwood, Lone Star flag, steer skull, string lights).** Rejected because it is the default look for any Texas bar plan an agent would produce without reading the brief closely, it would suit Melody Ranch in Waco or Texas T Pub in San Antonio just as well, and it ignores both the business's actual name and its coastal location entirely.
2. **Clean "modern gastropub" template (warm cream background, terracotta accent, high-contrast serif, three-column feature cards).** Rejected because it is the AI-slop default for any small-business site regardless of subject (see design-taste-frontend's premium-consumer palette warning), it would make a dive bar with pool tables and a patio band look like a downtown wine bar, and it actively works against the "unpretentious neighborhood bar" trust signal the reviews already establish.
3. **Nightlife/DJ-club direction (near-black background, single neon accent, glassmorphism cards, event-ticket UI).** Rejected because The Texan Drive-In is a pool-and-darts neighborhood bar with a patio band, not a cover-charge nightclub; a clubby UI would misrepresent the actual experience and would read as bait-and-switch to a first-time visitor standing at the door.

**Direction locked instead:** a mid-century roadside drive-in marquee sign (keyed to the business's actual name) fused with Gulf-port materiality (keyed to Corpus Christi specifically, not "Texas" generically). Full rationale in `design-system.md`.

## Non-goals for v0

- No online ordering, reservations, or payment
- No database, auth, or CMS
- No invented contact information of any kind
- No claims about pricing, cover charges, or hours

## Files in this repo

See `README.md` for the file index and `skills-used.md` for process notes.

  ]

# Page plan: Home (`/`)

Single most important page. Written to be understood cold from any of the three entry points in `user-flow.md` (search, shared link, review click-through), fully in under a phone-screen's worth of scrolling for the hero.

## 1. Nav (sticky, one line, max 72px tall)

- **Left:** wordmark lockup, "THE TEXAN DRIVE-IN" set as the marquee-letter-tile signature component (see `design-system.md`), small enough to sit in the nav without the flicker-on animation (that only plays once, in the hero, on first load)
- **Right:** three links max: "The Bar" -> `/the-bar`, "What's On" -> `/whats-on`, "Visit" -> `/visit`
- **No CTA button in the nav.** The hero carries both CTAs; a duplicate nav CTA would violate the no-duplicate-CTA-intent rule.
- Component: `NavBar` (custom, not shadcn default), background transparent over hero, solid `Channel Ink` once scrolled past hero (`useScroll` threshold, not a raw scroll listener).

## 2. Hero (fits in initial viewport, no scroll needed to see a CTA)

**Layout:** asymmetric split, `DESIGN_VARIANCE: 7`. Left column (55%): wordmark + headline + subhead + CTAs. Right column (45%): hero photo, teal-to-amber gulf-dusk gradient duotone treatment tying the two brand colors together over the image (see `assets.md` for sourcing/generation).

**Text stack (4 elements max, per hero-stack-discipline):**
1. Wordmark / brand mark (the marquee-letter component, not counted as an eyebrow)
2. Headline (H1): **"Pool, Darts, Shuffleboard, a Patio, and Live Bands on Weekends."**
3. Subhead (16 words): **"Rated 4.3 stars by more than 500 regulars on Google. See tonight's lineup and get directions below."**
4. CTAs: primary **"See What's On Tonight"** (-> `/whats-on`, Marquee Amber pill button), secondary **"Get Directions"** (-> `/visit#map`, outline pill button, Seafoam Porcelain border)

**Component:** `HeroSplit` + `MarqueeWordmark` (client component, isolated, only one with the flicker-on load animation). Mobile: stacks to single column, image moves below text, `min-h-[100dvh]` avoided on mobile (use `min-h-fit` so the hero does not force full-screen scroll on a small phone before the CTA is visible).

## 3. The Bar (games + patio) - condensed teaser, full detail lives on `/the-bar`

- **Headline:** "Pool Tables, Darts, Shuffleboard, and a Patio With Room to Spread Out."
- **Subhead:** "Walk in most nights and find an open table. On warm Gulf evenings, the patio fills up fast on weekends."
- **Component:** `PhotoFeatureRow` - one real/generated photo (patio or game area) left, text right on desktop; stacks on mobile. This is the ONE image+text-split section on the homepage (zigzag-alternation cap: max 2 in a row, and the homepage only needs one).
- **Link:** "See the whole bar" -> `/the-bar`

## 4. What's On (live music) - condensed teaser, full schedule lives on `/whats-on`

- **Headline:** "Live Bands Every Weekend, Right on the Patio."
- **Subhead:** "Bands play the patio most weekend nights. Show up, grab a seat, and see who's on tonight."
- **Component:** `MarqueeBoard` teaser - a small version of the same letter-tile marquee component, showing the current or next confirmed act, or a `[CONFIRM WITH OWNER: this weekend's lineup]` placeholder row if no schedule data exists yet. This reuses the hero's signature component instead of introducing a second visual language (deliberate repetition, not laziness: the marquee board is meant to feel like the same object doing its job twice).
- **Link:** "See this weekend's lineup" -> `/whats-on`

## 5. Reviews / trust

- **Headline:** "500 Google Reviews Averaging 4.3 Stars."
- **Subhead:** "Real reviewers rate the pool tables, the crowd, and the patio nights. Read what they say on Google and Yelp before you go tonight."
- **Component:** `ReviewStrip` - 2-3 short (max 3 lines each) real or owner-sourced review excerpts, attributed by first name + "Google review" or "Yelp review" (never invented full names presented as verified; if no real excerpt text is licensed for use yet, this section ships with the star/count stat only plus outbound links to the Yelp and Facebook pages, and the excerpt cards are marked `[PENDING: owner-approved review excerpts]`). No fabricated quotes ship under any circumstance.
- Outbound links: Yelp listing, Facebook page (both open in new tab, `rel="noopener noreferrer"`)

## 6. Footer

- Wordmark (small, static, no animation)
- Three nav links repeated (The Bar / What's On / Visit)
- Social links: Facebook, Instagram (icon only, from an allowed icon library, not hand-rolled SVG)
- Address line: `[STREET ADDRESS]` placeholder, styled in Plex Mono like a stenciled crate label
- No phone, no email, anywhere. If a contact method is added later by the owner, it goes here first as `[PHONE]` / `[BUSINESS EMAIL]` and must stay bracketed until a real, owner-confirmed value replaces it.
- Small print: "Concept site, pending business owner review." (Loop-3/pending-beta status marker, plain language, not a fake version-number footer.)

## Section-layout-repetition check

Layout families used on this page: `HeroSplit` (1), `PhotoFeatureRow` (2), `MarqueeBoard` teaser (3, distinct component), `ReviewStrip` (4, distinct component), footer (not counted as a content section). Four distinct families across four content sections: passes the repetition-ban comfortably; the homepage is short by design.

Zero uppercase-tracked eyebrow labels on this page (headline text alone carries each section, per the eyebrow-restraint rule). The only small-caps mono treatment is the footer address line, which is a data label, not a rhetorical eyebrow.

The final step in the flow from `user-flow.md`: the visitor is sold, now they need logistics. This page is the closest thing to a "contact page" this site has, and it deliberately has no contact form, phone number, or email address.

## 1. Sub-hero

- **Headline:** "Find The Texan Drive-In."
- **Subhead:** "Corpus Christi, Texas. Full directions and hours below."

## 2. Map

- **Component:** `MapEmbed`, anchor id `#map`, embedded map (e.g., Google Maps iframe) centered on `[STREET ADDRESS]` once the owner confirms it; ships with a placeholder pin over a generic Corpus Christi map view until then, clearly labeled in code comments as `TODO: replace with confirmed address`
- **Decorative detail:** the map pin uses `Buoy Red` (`#D1452B`), the one approved use of that color on the whole site, styled like a small channel-marker buoy rather than a generic teardrop pin
- **CTA:** "Open in Google Maps" (deep link, opens the visitor's own maps app with the address once confirmed)

## 3. Hours

- **Component:** `HoursTable` (simple two-column list, not a dense bordered table), all seven rows ship as `[HOURS: CONFIRM WITH OWNER]` until real hours exist. No invented hours, ever, including "typical bar hours."

## 4. Reviews and trust (the full version; the homepage carried the condensed teaser)

- **Headline:** "What the Reviews Say."
- **Component:** `ReviewGrid`, 4.3-star stat displayed large (Roboto Slab numeral, not a filled progress-bar widget), "~510 Google reviews" as the supporting line, plus outbound links to the Yelp listing and the Facebook page. Review excerpt cards ship only with owner-approved or verifiably public text; otherwise the section ships as stat-plus-links only, no placeholder quotes invented to fill space.

## 5. Follow along

- **Headline:** "Between Visits, Follow the Patio."
- **Component:** social link row, Facebook and Instagram, icon + label, no follower counts claimed unless verified

## Section-layout-repetition check

`PageIntro`, `MapEmbed`, `HoursTable`, `ReviewGrid`, social row: five sections, five distinct families, no repetition.

## Explicit no-invention rule for this page

This is the page most tempted to fabricate a phone number, email, or hours "to look complete." It must not. Every unconfirmed field ships bracketed and visible as unconfirmed, not silently filled with a plausible-looking fake value. This rule is restated in `implementation.md` so the Loop 3 build agent cannot miss it.

# GitHub workflow

## Branches

- **`dev`** - default branch. All Loop 2 plan content and all Loop 3 build work happen here first.
- **`prod`** - promotion target only. Starts as an empty branch pointing at the same initial commit as `dev`. Nothing merges into `prod` without a human explicitly promoting it after review; this campaign's authorization covers PR-to-`dev` merges, not `dev`-to-`prod` promotion.

## PR flow

1. All work happens on a feature branch cut from `dev` (e.g., `plan/homepage-copy-revision`, `build/hero-section`), never committed straight to `dev` once Loop 3 build work starts (Loop 2's initial plan content is the one exception, committed directly to `dev` as the repo's first commit, since there is nothing to review yet at repo creation).
2. Open a PR from the feature branch into `dev`.
3. CI must run and pass before requesting human review (see CI expectations below).
4. A human reviews and merges. No agent merges its own PR into `dev` without that review, even under a standing auto-merge authorization elsewhere, unless a human has separately authorized auto-merge for this specific repo.
5. Promotion from `dev` to `prod` is a separate, explicit, human-initiated action once the site is ready to go live; it is never bundled into a PR merge.

## CI expectations (to be wired in Loop 3, once there is code to check)

- Lint (ESLint/Next.js defaults) and typecheck (`tsc --noEmit`) on every PR
- Build must succeed (`next build`)
- Lighthouse (mobile) performance and accessibility checks, target ≥ 90 per `implementation.md`
- A grep-based secret/contact-leak check: fail CI if a phone-number-shaped or email-shaped string appears anywhere in tracked source that is not one of the literal bracket placeholders (`[PHONE]`, `[BUSINESS EMAIL]`) or this repo's own planning docs describing the rule

## Human review requirement

Every PR, whether Loop 2 plan revisions or Loop 3 code, requires a human look before merging into `dev`, and a separate, explicit human decision before promoting `dev` to `prod`. This repo currently has no code, so there is no CI to wire up yet; Loop 2's ten required plan files (listed in `README.md`) are committed directly to `dev` as the initial commit, per the campaign process (there is no reviewable diff before a repo exists). Any future Loop 2 revision to those files goes through the feature-branch-plus-PR flow above like any other change.

## Issue tracking

Use GitHub Issues for anything the owner needs to confirm before Loop 3 can finish a section (address, hours, band schedule, review-excerpt approval, photo-usage approval). Tag these `needs-owner-input` so they are easy to find separately from build bugs.

# texas-bar-texan-drive-in

Website **plan** (Loop 2 of the `website-pitch-pipeline` cold-outreach process) for **The Texan Drive-In**, a neighborhood bar in Corpus Christi, Texas. This repo is a pitch package, not a built site: the goal is a plan specific enough that (a) the owner would say yes to a real build, and (b) a Loop 3 agent could build it with zero follow-up questions.

## Status

**pending-beta.** Nothing has been built yet. This repo is Gate B material: a human reviews this plan before Loop 3 (the actual Next.js build) starts.

## Campaign

- **Campaign:** `texas-bars-batch-1`
- **Org:** PIIIX-org
- **Geography:** Texas, statewide campaign; this business specifically is Corpus Christi, TX (Gulf Coast)
- **Locale:** en-US

## Repo topics

`web-lead`, `pending-beta`, `batch-1`, `geo-texas`

Note: GitHub topics do not allow a colon character, so the campaign's `geo:<GEO_SLUG>` tagging convention is applied here as `geo-texas` instead of `geo:texas`. This substitution is specific to GitHub topic syntax; every other reference to the geography in this repo's prose uses `GEO_SLUG: texas` as given.

## What is actually in this repo

| File | What it covers |
|---|---|
| `brief.md` | Business facts, audience, geography, offer, conversion goal, rejected directions |
| `design-system.md` | Color, type, spacing, motion, and the "Carhop Marquee / Gulf Channel" visual lane, plus why it will not repeat elsewhere in the batch |
| `page-plans/home.md`, `the-bar.md`, `whats-on.md`, `visit.md` | Section-by-section IA, components, and final copy for each of the four planned routes |
| `assets.md` | What photo/logo material exists (Facebook/Yelp, rights-gated) vs. what gets generated (Pollinations prompts included) |
| `user-flow.md` | The visitor and owner flows this specific site is built around |
| `implementation.md` | The complete Loop 3 build prompt: stack, routes, components, performance/mobile rules, no-invented-contact-data rule |
| `handling-protocols.md` | Naming, resume-after-interruption, multi-agent handoff, sandboxed QA via `/browse`, token-cost notes |
| `github-workflow.md` | Branch strategy, PR flow, CI expectations, human review gates |
| `skills-used.md` | Which skills were actually invoked for this plan, why, and the self-score |

## How to pick this back up later

1. Read this README, then `brief.md`.
2. If nothing has changed about the business, proceed straight to Loop 3: hand `implementation.md` to a build agent as-is.
3. If the owner has confirmed any bracketed fact (address, hours, phone, email, band schedule, photo-usage rights), update `brief.md`'s verified-facts list first, then propagate the specific change into the relevant `page-plans/*.md` file(s) and `implementation.md`'s JSON-LD block. Do not silently fill a bracket without updating the source-of-truth file.
4. See `handling-protocols.md` for the full resume checklist and `github-workflow.md` for branch/PR mechanics.

## What this repo deliberately does not contain

No phone number, no email address, no invented street address, hours, or founding date. Every one of those facts is either absent or written as a literal bracket placeholder (`[PHONE]`, `[BUSINESS EMAIL]`, `[STREET ADDRESS]`, `[HOURS]`) throughout every file in this repo, including structured data in `implementation.md`.
